title: Incoming Engineer Setup Sprint + Feedback Protocol
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact hiring + onboarding artifact for IC engineering hires (senior and mid-level). It focuses on a short, structured "setup sprint" (day -7 through day 10) and an explicit feedback protocol to accelerate impact while capturing hire evidence for the first 90 days. Use this as the canonical lightweight checklist and rubric when recruiting, making offers, and running the 10-day setup sprint; complement with role-specific playbooks in Eng pods.

Audience:
- Hiring manager (HM) and hiring panel
- People Ops recruiter & onboarding coordinator
- Assigned buddy/mentor and tech mentor
- New hire (incoming engineer)

Goals:
1) Reduce early friction: fully provision dev access, run a build, and ship a tiny internal change in days 1–10.
2) Surface evidence for ramp decisions via structured artifacts and weekly checkpoints.
3) Improve acceptance velocity by providing a clear acceptance comms template and realistic week-one expectations.
4) Create consistent interview-to-onboard continuity (same rubric language in interview and onboarding feedback).

High-level timeline (compact):
- Preboarding (day -7 to -1): account creation, equipment ship, first readlist, intro comms.
- Day 0: orientation + environment smoke test.
- Days 1–3: pairing, first PR, shadow on-call or triage rotation.
- Days 4–10: ownership micro-sprint + demo to HM.
- Day 10 checkpoint: evidence packet + feedback sync.
- Week 2–4: expand ownership, regular retro cadence.
- Week 6 & 12: formal manager check-ins and calibrated eval.

Preboarding checklist (Recruiter / Onboarding coordinator responsibilities):
- Confirm offer acceptance and send preboarding packet within 24 hours. Packet includes: welcome note, team intro, first-week schedule, hardware tracking link, access list, and quick wins reading list.
- Trigger IT and SRE infra access templates (git, CI, internal VPN, issue tracker). Target: all accounts ready by Day 0.
- Assign buddy and tech mentor; coordinate calendar for shadowing.
- Share a tiny starter task (non-blocking) and a short README with build/run steps.
- Schedule day-0 1:1s (HM, buddy) on calendar.

Day 0 — smoke test and orientation (Manager / Buddy):
- Welcome + context (30m): HM shares team mission, current sprint goals, and expected outcomes for first 90 days.
- Environment smoke test (1h): clone repo, run tests, run local server or model pipeline for a minimal sequence. Document failures in the onboarding ticket.
- Admin: tools overview, Slack channels, calendar norms, payroll/benefits quick link.

First-10-day micro-sprint (goal: ship a small, safe change):
- Day 1–3: pairing pair-program on the starter task; create a small PR (lint + build + unit test).
- Day 4–7: independent follow-up work; mentor review cycles; address CI flakiness if encountered.
- Day 8–10: finish PR, demo to HM, merge, and confirm deploy pipeline (if applicable).
- Deliverable at day 10: merged PR or documented reason for delay + short writeup of what was learned and blockers.

Feedback protocol (format + cadence):
- Daily buddy check-ins (10–15m) for first 7 days; quick blockers log in the onboarding ticket.
- Day 10 checkpoint meeting (30m) between HM, mentor, and new hire. HM completes the "Day-10 evidence packet" template.
- Weekly 1:1s weeks 2–4, with a structured agenda: accomplishments, blockers, learning plan.
- Formal calibration at week 6 and week 12 (manager uses the same rubric as interviews).

Evidence packet (what HM/mentor must collect by Day 10):
- Link to PR(s) and short description (what changed, why).
- Build/test results and any follow-up tickets created.
- Self-assessment from new hire (1 paragraph: what went well, what’s hard).
- Buddy note: observed collaboration signals and learning velocity.

Interview rubric mapped to onboarding signals (use same axes during hiring and ramp):
- Problem decomposition (score 1–4): interviewer looks for structuring, tradeoff discussion, and clarity. Onboard signal: breaks down starter task and proposes incremental steps.
- System design / architecture thinking (1–4): during hire, evaluate tradeoffs and constraints; during ramp, look for design notes in PR and architecture questions asked.
- Code craft (1–4): clarity, tests, CI hygiene; onboard signal: PR has tests and a clear changelog.
- Communication & collaboration (1–4): async clarity, pairing behaviour; onboard signal: proactive updates, asks good clarifying questions.
- Ownership & impact orientation (1–4): seeks ways to reduce friction, creates tickets for follow-ups.
Scoring guidance: 4 = exceeds expectations for role level; 3 = ready with minor gaps; 2 = needs coaching; 1 = significant risk.

Acceptance comms template (Recruiter -> Candidate):
Subject: Welcome to Redwood — next steps and Day 0 logistics
Body: Hi [Name], welcome! We're excited you accepted. Your manager [HM name] will be in touch to share your Day 0 schedule. Expect hardware by [date]. Please complete the preboarding checklist sent to your email (link). For any questions ping me or your assigned buddy [buddy name] on Slack.
(Include links to payroll, benefits, and the Day-0 onboarding ticket).

Manager 90-day checklist (milestones):
- Week 2: new hire can run core dev loop and has made meaningful contributions to at least one task.
- Week 6: new hire owns a feature slice or operational task with minimal help.
- Week 12: new hire meets role expectations (>=3 on core rubric axes) or has a documented improvement plan.

Quick interview scheduling play (for recruiters):
- Two-stage panel for ICs hiring: take-home or pair exercise (4 days turnaround) + onsite panel (3 interviews: coding/architecture, system design, behavioral). Use rubric anchors and capture notes in the candidate record.
- Ideal panel composition: HM, senior IC from team, cross-functional partner (SRE or product), and a People Ops observer for calibration.

Risks & mitigations:
- Missing infra access: create an "access escalation" row in the onboarding ticket and notify infra lead; fallback: temporary VPN container image we can provide.
- First PR blocked by flaky CI: record flake and owner; prioritize temporary bypass (merge with green-check policy) and file follow-up ticket.
- Overloaded HM: delegate day-to-day escalate to buddy with clear escalation points.

Metrics we track for continuous improvement (people-ops + eng ops):
- Time to first PR merge (target: <= 10 days for majority of hires).
- Percent of hires with Day 0 full environment (target: 95%).
- New hire NPS at Day 10 and Day 30 (quick 3-question pulse).
- Offer-to-accept cadence (days) and acceptance rate by role.

Next steps & owners:
- People Ops: standardize Day-10 evidence packet and add to new hire checklist (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Infra: create a one-click HVAC VPN container for emergency access (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Eng managers: run pilot for 8 new hires using this compact sprint and report metrics after 60 days (owner: Leah Kim).

Appendix: practical templates (copy-paste)
- Buddy check-in micro-template (for Slack daily stand): "Hey [name] — quick check: green build? blockers? need pairing?"
- Day-10 evidence packet header: "Name / Role / PR links / Test status / Self note / Buddy note / HM assessment"
- Quick acceptance slack snippet for HM to post in team channel: "Team — please welcome [Name], joining as [Role] on [Date]. They’ll pair with [Buddy] this week. Please add a quick intro in #team-intros."

Notes / open questions (working):
- Should we experiment with a 48-hour mini-hack (day 6–7) to increase early impact? Pros/cons listed in comments.
- Consider adding a short culture ritual at Day 1 lunch (optional virtual trivia).

Document history: created 2025-11-02 by Aisha Patel; iterative updates and pilot notes through 2026-01-15.
